question.text: Under Section 135 read with CSR Rules, an independent impact assessment is MANDATORY for which of the following CSR projects — and this is typically the first formal engagement a SIA is invited to after SSE onboarding?

answer.text: Every CSR project regardless of outlay, provided the company is CSR-liable
Only CSR projects undertaken via a Section 8 FPE on the SSE (not trust/society implementers)
CSR projects of outlay INR 1 crore or more, that have been completed not less than one year before the impact assessment
Only multi-year ongoing projects of outlay above INR 10 crore

explanation.text: The Logic: Rule 8(3) of the Companies (CSR Policy) Rules 2014 mandates impact assessment through an independent agency for CSR projects with an outlay of INR 1 crore or more, that have been completed not less than one year before undertaking the impact study. This applies uniformly to companies with an average CSR obligation of INR 10 crore or more in the three immediately preceding financial years. For the SIA, this creates a steady pipeline of SAS-200/SAS-400/SAS-1300 engagements independent of whether the implementer is a trust, society or Section 8 FPE. The Trap: Not every project triggers impact assessment — only those above INR 1 cr. The obligation does not depend on the implementer's legal form. The INR 10 cr figure is a fabricated distractor (the real INR 10 cr test is on the DONOR'S 3-year avg obligation, not project outlay). Cross-Exam Context: X-A/X-B (Investment Adviser) touches CSR compliance; III-A/III-C touches LODR disclosure. XXIII specifically tests the impact-assessment trigger because it is the SIA's natural business development door with corporate donors. Assessor's Pro-Tip: When responding to a CSR impact-assessment RFP, confirm two dates upfront: (a) the project outlay crossing INR 1 cr, and (b) the project completion date being at least 12 months before your engagement. If either is missing, the assessment is voluntary, not mandatory — your scope, pricing, and the assurance level should reflect that difference.
